# phase-092 — Shard the test suite across parallel CI jobs

## You must change `.github/workflows/`

This phase declares `must_touch: [.github/workflows/]`. The gate fails the phase unless at
least one changed file falls under it. Writing tests, documentation or a report
is not enough — if you finish without touching that area, the phase fails on
exactly that check.


## Evidence — verified finding

```
One job runs everything. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `cargo build`, then `cargo test`, then clippy, then the README block executor, then the corpus count pin - serially, in a single job. The suite is 1,472 #[test] functions across src/ and tests/ plus 722 corpus files, and it grows every phase. A single job is a hard ceiling on how large the suite can become before a phase cannot finish inside its time limit, so the ceiling is currently a constraint on what the language is allowed to test. Cargo has no native sharding, so this has to be written, but it is the single largest lever available and it is pure CI configuration. NOTE: this phase changes .github/workflows/, and the rbops bot token deliberately has NO `workflows` permission (.github/workflows/rbops.yml:10) so that an agent cannot edit its own gate. An agent CANNOT land this phase. It is declared manual and is applied by a human push.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer
reproduces on `main`, stop and write that to `FINDINGS.md` — a stale phase must
never be "fixed" by inventing a change.

## Goal

Split `cargo test` across N parallel jobs using the matrix strategy, partitioning tests deterministically by a stable hash of each test name so every test runs in exactly one shard and the partition does not shift when unrelated tests are added. Add a final aggregation job that fails if any shard fails. Keep the fast jobs (build, clippy, fmt, README blocks, corpus pin) un-sharded so a formatting error is still caught in seconds rather than waiting on the slowest shard. Prove the partitioning is total and non-overlapping rather than assuming it. MANUAL: the agent that dispatches this must not attempt it; the change is pushed by a human with workflow scope.

## Method

1. Read `AGENTS.md` in full. Obey every hard rule; they are not negotiable.
2. Reproduce the finding. Record the exact command and the exact wrong output.
3. Write the failing test FIRST. Watch it fail. Do not touch production code
   until you have a red test that fails for the right reason.
4. Make the smallest change that turns it green.
5. Run the four gates yourself before claiming anything:

   ```bash
   cargo fmt --all -- --check
   cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
   cargo test --all-targets
   ./rbops/verify.sh phase-092
   ```

6. Write `REPORT.md` in the exact shape required by `AGENTS.md` section 4.

## Definition of done

- [ ] this phase is applied by a human push, not by the bot - an agent attempting it will have its push refused, which is the intended lock
- [ ] the suite runs across at least 4 parallel matrix jobs and the workflow shows the fan-out
- [ ] the union of shards runs every test exactly once - a test that asserts this by counting total tests per shard against the unsharded count, and it fails if any test is in two shards or none
- [ ] the shard assignment is stable: adding one new test changes only its own shard's membership, proven by a test over the partitioning function
- [ ] an aggregation job fails the workflow when any shard fails
- [ ] clippy, fmt and the README block executor still run in a fast job that does not wait for the shards
- [ ] the corpus-count pin still runs and still fails when README.md and the corpus disagree
- [ ] REPORT.md records the wall-clock before and after, measured from two CI runs on the same commit
